subject: amazon_s3_storage_billing_unit
extraction: visible text of the saved HTML with script and style removed, tags stripped, whitespace collapsed; the superscript exponents lost their markup, so '2 30' reads 2^30 and '2 40' reads 2^40
excerpt: Amazon S3 storage usage is calculated in binary gigabytes (GB), where 1 GB is 2 30 bytes. This unit of measurement is also known as a gibibyte (GiB), defined by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). Similarly, 1 TB is 2 40 bytes, i.e. 1024 GBs.
conclusion: S3 storage is billed per binary gigabyte: the catalog unit 'GB-Mo' means GiB-month, and 1 GB = 2^30 = 1,073,741,824 bytes.

corroboration.observation: The price list's own tier boundaries are begin_range 51200 (50 TB) and 512000 (500 TB), which are 50x1024 and 500x1024 GB, consistent with 1 TB = 1024 GB.

scope: S3 storage billed quantity only. The page's unit statement is not applied to EBS volume size, gp3 throughput, request counts or data transfer; each of those keeps its own source.
